reaudit_note: Mechanical re-stamp by `./le rfc reseal`. Every verdict re-stamped below was in the SHIFTED state: its recorded unit fingerprints -- the enclosing top-level function of each tagged test -- were byte-identical to the tree, and only the file around them had moved (a line shift, a sibling test, an import rewrite). Nothing about what any of these tests asserts changed, so no verdict was re-judged and only the `tests` map was rewritten. A verdict whose unit, cited producer code, or requirement text moved was REFUSED and left stale for a human. The proof is the code in verdict_freshness(), not this note.

RFC6138-4-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21. Positive TestRFC6138CutEdgeTransitLinkNotDelayed: not synchronized, no alternate path, the originated LSA keeps exactly 1 transit link. Negative TestRFC5443BroadcastCostOutCoversWholeSegment: the same not-synchronized segment with an alternate path is withheld. Records on IsCutEdge. TestLDPSyncTECostUntouched also pins ldpSyncWithholdTransit for cut-edge and non-cut-edge directly.

RFC6138-x-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-21. The precondition negative (SPF not yet run) is gone. Positive TestRFC6138PendingSPFRunBeforeCutEdgeAfterLinkLoss: the P2P links are withdrawn with a one-hour SPF pending, IsCutEdge answers true from the pending graph; negative TestRFC6138PendingSPFNeverLeavesStaleCutEdge: the reverse change answers false, never the stale true. TestLDPSyncCutEdgeUsesFreshSPF: a nil graph would answer true. Records on flushPendingSPF.
